### Minutes of Meeting

- Workshop — Resource Management Configuration (Master Data, Scheduling, Staffing, Rentals & AI Optimization)

### Date

- 26-August-2026

### Project

- TICVAI

### Meeting Type

- Product Workshop — Resource Management Configuration

### Prepared by

- Chitrangi Mestry

### Primary Objective

To walk through the resource management module in detail — resource master data and configuration, scheduling and calendar management, resource-to-event/package assignment models, staff/personnel management and rostering, equipment and rental management, and AI-driven resource optimization — so the team can align on configuration strategy ahead of build. The wallet module was deferred to the next session.

### Participants

- TICVAI Team

- Softlabs Team

### Agenda

- Resource management overview — command centre, calendar and revenue view

- Resource master data configuration — types, categories, profiles, attributes, hierarchy and dependency rules

- Package/bundle resource association and multi-venue resource management

- Resource calendar, scheduling and time-slot configuration

- Resource assignment models — pre-assigned vs. dynamic assignment at time of sale

- Conflict detection & resolution, multi-event planning and drag-and-drop allocation

- Staff/personnel resource management — profiles, skills, certifications and availability

- Workforce rostering, attendance, staffing control and AI-assisted staffing

- Dynamic resource assignment for experience tickets — skill matching, shared vs. private resources

- Equipment, assets and rental management

- AI resource optimization, staff mobile app and analytics/reporting

- Guest-facing booking behaviour and configuration Q&A

- Planning for the next session (wallet module)

### 4. Detailed Discussion

- 4.1 Resource Management Overview

Allam introduced the resource management command centre: a calendar-based overview showing the booking status of all resources (e.g., an instructor booked for a specific lesson, date and time), filterable by resource type and by venue, with a switchable revenue view.

- The overview can be viewed by day, week, month, or any custom period, giving a planner-style view of resource utilization across the business.

- 4.2 Resource Master Data Configuration

Resource types: any bookable/manageable entity — rooms, staff, equipment, vehicles, etc. — configured with capacity control and a reservable flag; the command centre shows total vs. active/assigned resources and their current availability status.

Categories & subcategories: resources can be grouped hierarchically (e.g., staff → employee/operations/instructor; equipment → lighting/sound; vehicles → SUV and other vehicle types), fully configurable rather than fixed.

- Resource profile: defines the resource name, category, capacity, active/inactive status, images and any category-specific details.

- Custom attributes: configurable per resource (e.g., capturing a vehicle's plate number so a specific vehicle instance can be assigned to a specific booking).

Resource hierarchy & relationships: resources can be linked in a main-resource / sub-resource structure (e.g., “vehicle” as a main resource type with a list of individual vehicles linked beneath it).

Dependency rules: resource requirements can be defined per product (e.g., a private ski lesson requires a minimum of two resources, or requires at least one vehicle) — the system enforces these dependencies when a resource-linked product is configured or sold.

Package/bundle configuration: multiple resources can be bundled together and linked to a single product (e.g., a VIP Cabana package bundling a room plus an attendant), so the system knows all resources required when that package is booked.

- Multi-venue resource management: covers how a resource that is used across multiple venues should be managed and shared.

Confirmed: in response to Chinmay's question, Allam confirmed that some elements of resource management configuration may be controlled at the tenant level rather than only centrally.

- 4.3 Resource Calendar & Scheduling

Resource calendar: an inquiry/planning screen showing resource availability by date range (e.g., which of 10 vehicles are available between a given start and end time), filterable and searchable across resource types.

- Resource schedule configuration: defines each resource's working pattern (e.g., available Monday–Friday, off on weekends) so planning and bookings respect real working availability.

Clarified: time slots are not created directly for resources — they are created for performances/events. Resources are then associated with those performance time slots, and once a performance is created, the system understands which resources should be available for it.

- 4.4 Resource Assignment Models

Two assignment models confirmed: (1) pre-assigned — specific resource instances (e.g., a named vehicle, a named instructor, a specific room) are mapped directly to a time slot in advance, so a booking against that slot automatically receives the pre-assigned resources; and (2) dynamic — only the resource type and quantity are defined (e.g., “one SUV vehicle and one guide”), and the system checks availability and assigns an actual available resource automatically at the time of sale.

Reservation/blocking of a specific resource outside of a normal sale is only needed for exceptional cases (e.g., deliberately holding a resource for a future booking); in the standard flow, resources are booked automatically as a consequence of the associated package being sold — the guest does not book the resource directly.

- Confirmed: the system must validate resource bookings and prevent the same resource from being double-booked or assigned to overlapping bookings (conflict detection and resolution).

- Multi-event resource planning and drag-and-drop resource allocation allow resources to be assigned to events visually, in addition to rule-based automatic assignment.

- 4.5 Staff / Personnel Resource Management

Personnel (cashiers, trainers, drivers, and other staff) are managed as a resource type, with a command-centre view of total personnel, how many are on duty, available, or on leave.

A resource profile's operational summary shows associated bookings; the same booking information is mirrored on a staff-facing employee mobile app, so staff can see their tasks/bookings for the day directly on their phone.

Skills & competency management: defines the qualifications/certifications required for a resource to be eligible for a given role (e.g., level 1/2/3 ski-instructor certification required to qualify as an advanced-level trainer).

- Certification expiry management: tracks certification documents and validity periods (e.g., annual renewal), flagging when recertification is due.

Staff availability and shift templates (morning/afternoon/evening) define working patterns; the system recognizes which shift a staff member has logged into based on configured shift timings.

Leave/absence configuration covers leave types and quotas, functioning similarly to a lightweight HR module, with an option to integrate with an external HR or third-party time-and-attendance system if required.

- 4.6 Workforce Rostering, Attendance & Staffing Control

- A staffing dashboard shows checked-in, on-shift, on-leave, open-shift and closed-shift counts based on check-in/check-out logs, along with staffing cost tracking (including overtime).

A roster/tapping view per resource shows required vs. scheduled vs. checked-in counts for the day, surfacing discrepancies (e.g., 10 ski trainers scheduled, only 8 checked in).

- Minimum staffing/coverage rules can be set per venue and day (e.g., a minimum number of instructors required per level), driven by the planner.

Gap handling: if a scheduled resource fails to check in, the system flags the shortfall for operations follow-up, and can use AI to recommend reassigning that resource's bookings to another available resource.

Swap requests allow a staff member going on break to request coverage from another resource; attendance exceptions/adjustments can be manually marked (active, not active, absent, or other exceptions).

A compliance/validation centre flags events where required staffing is not met (e.g., staff required but not yet checked in), and the module tracks associated labour cost.

- An AI workflow layer supports staffing/resource-planning optimization on top of the above.

- 4.7 Dynamic Resource Assignment for Experience Tickets

Recap: resources are bundled to an event/package (as in 4.2); when a performance is created for that event, the system checks resource availability and assigns accordingly.

Staff experience/qualification mapping: an event can require a specific qualification level (e.g., an advanced instructor only, excluding intermediate/beginner) — the system enforces this mapping rather than assigning any qualified-looking staff member.

Resource combination builder: for a given event, defines the required resource types, quantities, and whether each is mandatory or optional (e.g., an instructor, an area, and a set of equipment).

Ticket demand & resource planning: resource allocation can be fixed-quantity, or ratio-based/dynamic — the system can add resources dynamically as sales volume increases, based on configured rules, rather than only using a fixed pre-set number of resources.

Ratio-based example: a single tour guide can be configured to accommodate up to a defined number of guests/tickets (e.g., up to 10 tickets per tour), so the system does not require one resource per guest.

- Channel-based resource assignment: configuration can determine whether resources are auto-assigned by type or specifically allocated, and this can vary by sales channel.

Confirmed (Chinmay): skill-based resource matching should rely on straightforward keyword/attribute matching (e.g., skill level, language) rather than a full AI-based matching system, to avoid unnecessary complexity.

Resource sharing models: a resource can be one-to-one (dedicated to a single booking) or one-to-many/shared (e.g., a meeting room with multiple bookable pods, or a shared vehicle resource booked across sequential time slots) — the system must block further sales once a shared resource's capacity or time slot is fully booked, and release it again if a booking is cancelled.

Decision: resource allocation should rotate across all available resources (e.g., resource 1, then 2, then 3) rather than repeatedly reusing the same resource, to avoid overburdening any single resource while others remain unused.

- Priority allocation policy: the system should support automatic replacement/reassignment if an assigned resource becomes unavailable.

- 4.8 Equipment, Assets & Rental Management

Rental item management (e.g., strollers, wheelchairs, towels): tracks inventory and quantity per day, records check-out and check-in of items, and updates inventory automatically on return.

- Deposit handling: supports capturing a refundable deposit (with guest details) at the time of rental, and processing the refund on return.

Usage-based billing: supports calculating excess charges at return based on actual usage duration versus the period originally paid for (e.g., a wheelchair rented for one hour but used for three is charged for the additional two hours at return).

- Maintenance state: an item can be marked out-of-maintenance/faulty so it is excluded from available inventory until resolved.

Confirmed (Chinmay): rental/equipment items can be tracked with simplified state attributes (e.g., available, rented, faulty) rather than requiring granular custom attributes for this category — agreed by Allam.

Confirmed: rental item and inventory data is expected to be provided by each client during onboarding, with a screen provided to update inventory and item details thereafter.

- 4.9 AI Optimization, Mobile App & Analytics

AI-based resource optimization and forecasting: based on historical booking/sales data, the system can recommend staffing levels for upcoming periods (e.g., “you will need this many resources over the next week”) so leave and availability can be planned accordingly.

Employee mobile app: staff see their assigned bookings and tasks, perform check-in/check-out and shift closing, and can request a swap (e.g., for break coverage) directly from the app.

- Analytics & reporting: covers total cost and revenue by resource and by event, across all resource-management activity.

- 4.10 Guest-Facing Behaviour & Configuration Q&A

Confirmed: a guest always books a product or package — never a resource directly, and never a specific room/vehicle/instructor by itself — across all sales channels. The product's configuration determines which resources are associated and get booked behind the scenes.

Dynamic pricing example: a bookable resource such as a meeting room can be priced per hour, with the system calculating total price from the booked duration and blocking that room for the booked window so it cannot be double-booked by another guest.

Raised (Aishwarya): whether merchandise/retail purchases should complete entirely within the TICVAI platform, citing an example from another marketplace app that required downloading a separate app to complete a purchase.

Decision: food & beverage and retail/merchandise online sale remain optional, back-office-enabled modules, but where enabled, the entire purchase flow (browse, cart, checkout, and choice of pickup-at-venue or ship-to-guest) must complete within the TICVAI platform — guests should not be redirected to download a separate app to complete a purchase.

- Raised (Qossai): whether a guest can choose a specific instructor when booking a private lesson (e.g., for Ski Dubai), versus one being auto-assigned.

Decision: instructor/resource selection will be a configurable, per-ticket-type setting — private-session ticket types can optionally allow the guest to choose a specific instructor, while group-session ticket types auto-assign an instructor without exposing the choice to the guest. Private and group sessions are modelled as two separate products with separate pricing, not variants of the same product.

Chinmay raised the related configuration question of how a customer-initiated request for a private session against a resource that normally serves shared/group sessions (e.g., requesting a private lesson with an instructor who usually runs group lessons) should be handled; resolved (Qossai/Allam) as: this is modelled as a distinct, separately configured and separately priced product, rather than an ad hoc request raised against the shared/group product.

Question (Chitrangi): can a guest rent a resource directly from the guest/mobile app? Allam confirmed: no — a guest books a product (e.g., a meeting room product, or an experience package), and the product's configuration determines which resources are associated and get booked; guests do not book raw resources directly.

Allam shared a reference website (a Sharjah library's meeting-room/“pod” booking flow and tiered membership plans) as an example of a simple duration-based booking flow without fixed performances/time slots, for the team to review as UX inspiration.

### 5. Key Decisions & Agreements

- Wallet module walkthrough deferred to the next session (tomorrow, same time).

Resource assignment will support two models — pre-assigned (mapped ahead of time) and dynamic (assigned at time of sale based on real-time availability) — both required in the system.

- Guests always book a product/package; resources are never booked directly by a guest, across all sales channels.

- Merchandise/F&B/retail online sale, where enabled, must complete entirely within the TICVAI platform without redirecting guests to a separate app download.

Instructor/resource selection will be a per-ticket-type configuration — enabled for private-session products, disabled (auto-assign) for group-session products — with private and group sessions modelled as two distinct, separately priced products.

- Skill-based resource matching will use straightforward attribute/keyword matching (skill level, language) rather than a full AI-matching system.

- Resource allocation should rotate across available resources rather than repeatedly reusing the same one, to avoid overburdening any single resource.

- Rental/equipment items will be tracked with simplified state attributes (available, rented, faulty, out-of-maintenance) rather than granular custom attributes.

### 6. Open Items / Questions for Follow-Up

- Detailed resource-management reference document covering each configuration area discussed today — pending from Allam.

- Existing hardware/ticketing-system documentation (shared earlier by Qossai), which also covers resource planning/templates but excludes staffing/check-in-out functionality — to be reviewed by the Softlabs team.

- Any additional follow-up questions on the resource management module — to be compiled by Chinmay and routed to Qossai.

- House of Wisdom (Sharjah) meeting-room/POD booking and membership-tier flow — to be reviewed as a UX reference.

## 2026-08-27

`sources/mom/TICVAI_MoM_2026-08-27_WalletConfiguration.docx` · 2,796 words

### Minutes of Meeting

- Workshop — Wallet, Funding & Stored Value Configuration (Wallet Types, Top-Up, Family Wallets, Gift Cards & Fraud Controls)

### Date

- 27-August-2026

### Project

- TICVAI

### Meeting Type

- Product Workshop — Wallet, Funding & Stored Value Configuration

### Prepared by

- Chitrangi Mestry

### Primary Objective

To walk through the wallet module in detail — wallet foundation and types, funding/top-up and reload management, stored value and credit-consumption logic, family/parent-child and corporate wallets, gift cards and vouchers, wallet payments and transfers, and fraud/risk and API governance — so the team can align on configuration strategy ahead of build.

### Participants

- TICVAI Team

- Softlabs Team

### Agenda

- Wallet foundation and dashboard overview

- Wallet type library, ownership and account association

- Currency, credit types and wallet feature profile

- Wallet lifecycle, numbering and publish flow

- Funding, top-up and reload management

- Stored value, credit consumption and FEFO (first-expiry-first-out) logic

- Split-tender payments, redemption rules and configuration simulation

- Family, parent-child and corporate wallets

- Gift cards, vouchers and wallet payments

- Transfers, fraud/risk controls and finance reconciliation

- API integration and third-party POS governance

- Planning for the next session and other project updates

### 4. Detailed Discussion

- 4.1 Wallet Foundation & Dashboard

Allam introduced the wallet foundation screen — defining the types of wallets to be set up and how wallet configuration works overall — alongside a dashboard giving an overview of all live wallet balances: total wallet value, total spend, and total recharge activity.

Confirmed: wallet balances are tied to revenue recognition. Money loaded by a customer is initially recorded as a liability; once the balance is consumed against a specific product/service, it is recognized against that product's revenue account.

- 4.2 Wallet Type Library, Ownership & Account Association

Wallet type library: multiple wallet types can be created based on business need (e.g., guest wallet, family wallet, membership wallet), each assignable to a category (individual, corporate, member, etc.).

Wallet creation & provisioning rules define the trigger point at which a wallet is created — e.g., on membership purchase, or on completing a top-up transaction. Two general patterns were discussed: a gift-card style wallet (pre-defined, purchasable value products listed on the website) and an “add money to wallet” style wallet (open-ended top-up against a guest profile).

Wallet ownership & account association: defines who owns and controls a wallet. In a family example, a parent can add money to the wallet while children can view the balance and spend but cannot top up — access rules are configurable per wallet type.

- 4.3 Currency, Credit Types & Wallet Feature Profile

Currency & balance configuration: defines which currencies are supported for a given wallet, along with maximum balance rules. Local-currency top-up (cash or card) is the general case; foreign-currency top-up (e.g., USD) is supported via a configured exchange rate that converts and credits the wallet in local currency.

Credit & balance-type configuration: defines the types of value that can be stored — e.g., cash credit, different credit, bonus credit, gift-card credit — each classified as monetary (usable as general spendable funds) or non-monetary (an entitlement/redemption credit with no stored monetary value, e.g., a meal voucher redeemable only for a specific item).

Wallet feature profile: a global (and optionally wallet-type-specific) configuration of which actions are permitted — e.g., top-up allowed, refund allowed. Example: a membership-benefit credit (e.g., a AED 100 voucher granted with membership purchase) can be configured as spendable but not refundable/cashable-out, since it was granted as a benefit rather than loaded by the customer.

- 4.4 Wallet Lifecycle, Numbering & Publish Flow

- Wallet lifecycle configuration tracks status from creation to expiry/closure — active, suspended, blocked, or closed.

Confirmed: every wallet requires a validity period; it cannot remain open indefinitely. Once the validity period lapses, any remaining balance is automatically swept to a finance-designated account, per policy — this applies to monetary balances as well as non-monetary credits/vouchers, not only to points-style rewards.

Wallet numbering: each wallet is issued a unique wallet code (similar to a ticket number), with configurable association to physical/digital media — QR code, RFID, or other media types.

- A final review/publish screen summarizes the completed wallet-type configuration (rules, applicable channels) before it is published live.

- 4.5 Funding, Top-Up & Reload Management

- A top-up dashboard shows all wallet top-ups (successful or failed) and funding-by-source breakdowns (credit card, debit card, cash, etc.), with totals by day/month/year.

- Funding method configuration defines which payment methods (cash, card, online, POS, kiosk self-service) are supported for adding money to a wallet.

Clarified (manual admin funding): this is a payment method used, for example, to issue a goodwill/service-recovery credit to a guest's wallet (e.g., where service fell short of expectations), rather than a standard customer-initiated top-up.

- Raised (Chinmay): role-based permissions for staff funding wallets, and how a manual top-up reconciles against the finance ledger.

Confirmed: every financial transaction (revenue, payment, tax, wallet top-up) is tied to a chart-of-account entry, so P&L and balance-sheet reporting can correctly reflect assets, liabilities, income and expenses — e.g., total wallet balances outstanding are reported as a liability owed to customers.

- Top-up rule configuration sets minimum and maximum top-up amounts (e.g., a variable top-up with a configured minimum, and a maximum cap per transaction).

- Channel & funding-source mapping restricts which payment methods are available on which channel (e.g., cash top-up allowed only on-site, not online).

Auto-reload configuration: proposed as a feature where a wallet automatically tops up by a configured amount once the balance falls below a threshold. Allam flagged this as a nice-to-have without a confirmed real-world use case yet; Chinmay agreed it is still worth including for higher-value/frequent guests who prefer not to manage top-ups manually.

Recurring funding schedule: a separate, calendar-based scheduled top-up (e.g., a fixed amount added every Monday), distinct from auto-reload since it is triggered by date rather than by balance threshold.

Requested (Chinmay): both auto-reload and recurring funding schedules should be configurable by the guest themselves via the guest/web app, not only by venue admins on the back end.

Funding authorization & approval rules define when a top-up requires supervisor or finance approval (e.g., approval required above a configured threshold amount, via supervisor login).

Reversal (void transaction): supports full or partial reversal of a top-up, with funds returned to the original payment method. Chinmay confirmed this should require manual verification/authorization before processing, which Allam agreed is required.

- Funding limits & velocity controls set daily, monthly, minimum and maximum transaction thresholds to prevent excessive or suspicious top-up activity.

- A funding transaction audit trail shows all top-up transactions for any given period or account.

- 4.6 Stored Value, Credit Consumption & FEFO Logic

Requested (Chinmay): Chinmay shared that six wallet types had already been scoped on the Softlabs side (including attraction credit, game credit, rental credit, parking credit, and other credit types), and asked Allam to send the wallet-configuration documentation so these can be cross-checked and expanded against it — Allam confirmed he will share this.

Credit type definition and credit issue rule configuration recap how credits are granted — e.g., a purchase (membership, product, or experience) can trigger issuance of a credit governed by rules set at the wallet/credit-type level.

Credit usage restrictions allow a credit to be scoped to specific spend categories (e.g., a credit usable only for food & beverage and not valid for retail), fully configurable per business need; where no restriction is set, the balance can be spent on any offered product or service.

Consumption priority engine — FEFO (first-expiry-first-out): wallet balances loaded at different times can carry different expiry dates; when a guest spends from the wallet, the system automatically consumes the balance with the nearest expiry date first, without requiring the guest to choose which “lot” to spend from.

Clarified: in response to Chinmay's question on whether guests should be able to select which wallet/credit to consume from, Allam confirmed consumption is fully automatic based on the FEFO logic — guests can see their balance and expiry breakdown per transaction/lot in their profile, but cannot manually choose which lot is drawn down.

Bonus credit example: gaming/top-up incentive tiers (e.g., a AED 100 top-up earns a AED 20 bonus credit, a AED 200 top-up earns AED 60) — bonus credit is consumed before the base top-up credit and carries its own separate validity period.

A worked FEFO example was walked through: three top-up transactions on different dates, each with a different expiry date; when the guest spends, the system consumes from the earliest-loaded (nearest-expiry) transaction first, then the next, and so on.

- 4.7 Split-Tender, Redemption Rules & Configuration Simulation

Split tender / multi-credit consumption: a single purchase can be paid using a combination of wallet balance plus another payment method (e.g., card) — for example, AED 500 from the wallet and the remaining AED 200 of a AED 700 purchase charged to a credit card.

Partial vs. full redemption: some wallet/gift-card types can be configured to allow partial redemption (spend part of the balance, retain the remainder), while others can be configured to require full redemption in a single transaction (no partial use).

- Credit expiry & extension operations give admins a customer-level view of all wallet balances and their expiry dates, to manage upcoming expiries.

Configuration simulation tool: in response to Chinmay's question, Allam explained this is a test/simulation mode that lets an admin validate a wallet configuration (e.g., spend-category restrictions) by running sample transactions before publishing it live — avoiding the need to publish first and discover configuration errors through live testing.

- 4.8 Family, Parent-Child & Corporate Wallets

Family/parent-child wallets: a parent's wallet can fund linked child wristbands/wallets without the child needing a separate top-up; the parent can configure per-child spending allowances (e.g., of a AED 500 family balance, one child is capped at AED 200 and another at AED 200).

- Confirmed: guests can create family-member profiles themselves and configure spending limits directly from their own guest account, in addition to venue-side configuration.

Family permission rules: a parent/guardian is typically the only member allowed to top up the family wallet; children can view balances and transactions and spend, but cannot top up, unless permissions are explicitly reconfigured.

- Corporate/group wallets: funds can be loaded and segregated across departments (e.g., marketing, operations) for corporate/company accounts.

Shared wallet transfer: balance can be moved between linked wallets in either direction (parent → child or child → parent) within a family or group structure — confirmed as a configurable, venue-controlled feature rather than always enabled.

- 4.9 Gift Cards, Vouchers & Wallet Payments

Gift cards and vouchers follow similar mechanics to the wallet, with two variants: a monetary gift card (redeemable as general value against any product/service the venue offers) and a product-specific gift voucher (an entitlement redeemable only against a named product/experience, e.g., a dolphin-show voucher, not exchangeable for value against other products).

- Redemption channel configuration determines whether a gift card/voucher can be redeemed online, on-site, or both.

Wallet payments: spend can be reported by department/category (F&B, attractions, retail, partners) and by channel (B2C, POS); wallet payment/redemption policy defines rules such as minimum spend to use wallet as a payment method.

- Wallet-to-media linking associates a wallet with its supporting media — RFID/wristband, QR code, or other identifiers — for use across channels.

- 4.10 Transfers, Fraud/Risk Controls & Finance Reconciliation

Unload/refund: a guest can redeem/unload a remaining wallet balance at end of visit (e.g., at a counter, after a balance check) rather than keeping it loaded.

Peer-to-peer transfer: supports transferring balance from one guest's wallet directly to another guest's wallet. Chinmay confirmed this, like the unload/refund flow, should be a configurable, venue-level toggle (allowed or not allowed) rather than a default always-on feature — agreed by Allam.

- Wallet risk policy configuration bundles validity, expiry and refund rules per wallet policy.

Transaction risk scoring engine: assigns a risk score to transactions to flag potentially fraudulent or suspicious activity. In response to Chinmay's question on what action follows a high risk score, Allam confirmed flagged transactions are routed to the operations team for manual cross-verification rather than being auto-approved or auto-declined by the system.

Lost-media recovery: if a guest loses a wristband/card with a loaded balance, the operations team can identify the guest (e.g., via phone number or ID), locate the original transaction, and transfer the balance to a replacement wristband/card.

Finance, liability and reconciliation (recap): every wallet transaction ties back to the chart of accounts, so finance can report total outstanding liability, revenue recognized, and related balances at any time.

- 4.11 API Integration & Third-Party POS

Wallet APIs support two integration patterns: (1) external systems consuming TICVAI's wallet API directly to check balance and process a transaction, with the wallet balance updated in the system afterward; and (2) integration with a third-party F&B/retail POS system (e.g., Micros, Symphony) at a venue, where the third-party system consumes the wallet API to verify sufficient balance and process a transaction, with the balance reduced accordingly on completion.

- 4.12 Planning & Other Project Updates

- Qossai left the session early to attend another meeting; Allam confirmed the remaining walkthrough would continue without him.

Chinmay confirmed the B2C ticketing website flow (product creation and add-to-cart) referenced in a prior session is still being revised, led by Aishwarya, and will be shared once finalized.

Planned: Chinmay and Pradnya will prepare three separate wireframe flows — general ticketing, F&B, and retail — to be shared for review ahead of full UI/UX build, so that any structural issues can be corrected early. Chinmay targeted sharing these by next Wednesday.

Open: the next session was proposed for tomorrow, same time, to continue with additional topics, but a public holiday falls on that date for at least one side's team. Chinmay will confirm via WhatsApp with senior team members whether to proceed tomorrow or reschedule to Monday.

### 5. Key Decisions & Agreements

- Wallet validity/expiry rules apply to monetary balances as well as non-monetary credits and vouchers; expired balances are automatically swept to a finance-designated account.

Wallet balance consumption follows an automatic, system-driven FEFO (first-expiry-first-out) model — guests can view balances and expiry breakdown but cannot manually select which lot is spent from.

- Bonus/promotional credit is consumed before base top-up credit and carries its own separate validity period.

- Split-tender payments (wallet plus another payment method in a single transaction) and configurable partial vs. full redemption will both be supported.

- A configuration simulation/test tool will be included so wallet rule configurations can be validated before publishing live.

Family and corporate wallet structures will support parent-controlled top-up with configurable, per-member spend allowances; guests can also self-configure family profiles and limits from their own account.

- Peer-to-peer wallet transfers and end-of-visit balance unload/refund will both be configurable, venue-level toggles rather than default always-on features.

- All wallet transactions (top-up, spend, refund, expiry sweep) are tied to the finance chart of accounts for liability and revenue reporting.

- High-risk-scored transactions are flagged for manual review/cross-verification by the operations team rather than handled automatically.

- Auto-reload (balance-threshold-triggered) and recurring funding (calendar-scheduled) should both be configurable by the guest via the guest/web app, not only by venue admins.

### 6. Open Items / Questions for Follow-Up

- Detailed wallet-configuration reference documentation — pending from Allam.

- Cross-check of the six previously-scoped wallet types (attraction, game, rental, parking, and other credits) against Allam's documentation — pending from Chinmay.

- Auto-reload feature — real-world use case/demand still to be validated; currently a nice-to-have rather than a confirmed requirement.

- Revised B2C ticketing website flow (product creation and cart) — in progress with Aishwarya, pending share-out once finalized.

- Three wireframe flows (general ticketing, F&B, retail) — targeted for delivery by next Wednesday.

- Confirmation of tomorrow's session (public holiday) vs. rescheduling to Monday — pending from Chinmay via WhatsApp.

### Minutes of Meeting

- Workshop — Customer Service, B2B/Resale & OTAs, Communications, Group Sales, Waivers, Product Governance & Sales Channels

### Date

- 31-August-2026

### Project

- TICVAI

### Meeting Type

- Product Workshop — Customer Service, B2B/Resale, Group Sales & Sales Channel Configuration

### Prepared by

- Chitrangi Mestry

### Primary Objective

To walk through several remaining product modules in one extended session — customer service/contact center, B2B reseller and OTA management, centralized communications, group and corporate sales, waiver/consent forms, product lifecycle governance, and sales channel/pricing configuration — covering as much ground as possible, with any remaining modules to continue in subsequent daily sessions.

### Participants

- TICVAI Team

- Softlabs Team

### Agenda

- Customer service and contact center — case management

- Contact center operations, AI routing and quality management

- B2B reseller and OTA partner management

- B2B commercial agreements, credit and payment models

- B2B day-to-day operations and settlement

- Communications and notifications (centralized module)

- Group sales and corporate/school bookings

- Group operations, payment links and check-in

- Product lifecycle, catalog and change governance

- Sales channel, pricing and inventory allocation

- Resale marketplace

- UX reference walkthrough (Little Explorer, Dubai) and payment gateway approach

- Planning for upcoming sessions

### 4. Detailed Discussion

- 4.1 Customer Service & Contact Center (Case Management)

Allam introduced the case management and contact center module, used by customer-service agents to log and manage customer-reported issues. A dashboard shows total cases logged, due cases, and per-agent case load, each governed by an SLA based on case type.

A customer profile screen gives agents a single view of a customer's details, open cases, and case history; a communications & transactions screen shows the full history of prior communications and actions logged against that profile.

Case creation captures the logging channel/source, category and subcategory (e.g., ticket issue → reschedule), and supports screenshot attachments; case investigation & resolution tracks all activity and actions taken against a case.

Agents can view and act on a customer's bookings/tickets directly from the case screen (e.g., date change, reschedule, resend tickets), and can initiate refunds/compensation, route requests for internal approval, or raise an internal escalation to another department (visible on that department's mobile app).

- Once resolved, agents log the resolution outcome; an AI customer-service summarizer compiles all actions taken on a case for quick review.

- 4.2 Contact Center Operations, AI Routing & Quality Management

A supervisor-level dashboard gives an overview of the entire contact center — case volume by category (general support, refund, ticketing, membership, etc.) and current status.

Intelligent routing: cases are automatically routed to the most suitable agent or department based on skill set, language, availability, workload and priority, with an assignment preview that can be manually overridden before confirming.

SLA policies are configurable per case type; agent workload views allow cases to be reassigned to balance load across agents; escalation and case monitoring allow unresolved cases to be escalated further.

Quality management scores agent performance based on resolution time and outcome against the SLA; customer satisfaction survey results and week-over-week case volume trends are also tracked on the dashboard.

- 4.3 B2B Reseller & OTA Partner Management

An overview screen shows all B2B partners, their status, pending approvals and documentation state. A partner profile captures company information and a configurable partner category/type, with the underlying fields fully customizable per business need.

Partner onboarding & application workflow tracks a partner from initial sign-up (via a registration link/form on the B2B platform) through review and approval, with confirmation emails and back-office visibility into required next steps.

Partner contacts support multiple agents/sub-agents per partner (e.g., a main agent and sub-agents who can each sell on the partner's behalf); territory/market and distribution rights define which regions a partner may sell into; brand/venue association defines which venues and products a partner can sell, supporting multi-venue setups with distinct pricing per venue.

Partner documentation & compliance repository manages required documents (e.g., trade license, VAT certificate) with a review/accept/reject/resubmit workflow; partner access controls define which actions a partner may perform (e.g., refund, reschedule); partner approval status tracks the lifecycle from lead → submitted → active → suspended; a partner 360 view consolidates all of the above.

Clarified (integration models): Qossai outlined two integration approaches for B2B/OTA partners — (1) the partner uses the TICVAI B2B portal directly (a white-label-style B2B credential, similar to B2C) with no integration complexity; or (2) integration with external OTAs (e.g., Ticketmaster, Platinum List, BookMyShow) via API, which is the preferred direction, with commission charged per ticket sold through that channel. Some large OTAs may require the venue/TICVAI to integrate into their systems instead of the reverse — the platform needs to support both directions.

Clarified: once an OTA integration exists for one client, activating it for a new client (who separately signs a commercial agreement with that OTA) should only require enabling the existing integration, not rebuilding it.

Additional option confirmed: for partners who do not want to integrate via API, TICVAI can issue a bulk batch of pre-generated tickets (with QR codes, at agreed rates, valid for a defined period) as a CSV export for the partner to import into their own platform and resell independently, without live API consumption.

- 4.4 B2B Commercial Agreements, Credit & Payment Models

An agreements overview shows all active and pending B2B agreements; each agreement captures term/value, and partner-specific pricing — discounts can be configured by quantity, amount, percentage, or tiered volume bands (e.g., 10% up to 1,000 tickets, 15% from 1,000–5,000).

- Commission/margin configuration defines the commission rate a partner earns per ticket sold.

Three payment models confirmed: (1) credit limit — a partner sells up to an approved credit ceiling, invoiced periodically (monthly) and settled by cheque or bank transfer; (2) prepayment/advance — a partner pre-funds a wallet-style balance (via bank transfer or online top-up) and draws it down per sale, topping up as needed; and (3) pay-per-transaction by card.

Commercial/inventory allocation allows a defined quantity of inventory to be reserved specifically for a partner; booking limits cap the maximum tickets per transaction or transactions per day, configurable per partner or overall.

- A consolidated partner overview screen shows profile, agreement, and payment information together in one view.

- 4.5 B2B Day-to-Day Operations & Settlement

- An operations dashboard shows each partner's order volume, revenue, reservations, and any tickets on hold (booked but not yet issued).

Partner cancellations and refund requests, partner statement of account (opening/closing balance, transaction activity), and reconciliation/exception management (for manual postings or unsettled bank transfers) are all tracked from this view, along with dispute handling.

- An AI-driven partner performance view surfaces trends, risks and opportunities across the partner base to support account management decisions.

- 4.6 Communications & Notifications

Confirmed (Qossai): communications and notifications will be built as a single centralized module that all other modules plug into, rather than each module building its own notification logic independently.

A dashboard shows communication activity across channels (email, WhatsApp, SMS) — delivered, pending, failed. Channel & provider configuration covers SMTP setup for email, SMS gateway configuration, and WhatsApp provider configuration; sender identity/domain configuration governs the from-address and reply-to address per brand (e.g., no-reply@venue.com, customerservice@venue.com).

- Templates are fully configurable per channel (email, SMS, WhatsApp) — header, logo, footer, and content — for consistent branded communications.

Business event & notification triggering: trigger conditions can be based on precise event states rather than the transaction alone — e.g., a post-visit survey should be triggered only when a ticket was actually scanned/used (attended), not simply purchased, whereas a “how was your experience” follow-up can instead be triggered off the sale itself. Routing/fallback rules define an alternate channel if a message fails to deliver.

- Consent & communication preference tracking records marketing/newsletter opt-in status per customer; the delivery queue tracks failed sends and supports automatic retry until successful delivery.

- Noted (Chinmay): this reporting could be extended with an AI-generated monthly marketing report, similar to the AI reporting capability discussed for other modules.

- 4.7 Group Sales & Corporate/School Bookings

A sales-team dashboard shows group inquiries, opportunities and confirmed bookings, and flags items needing attention. Customer categorization supports individual (B2C/walk-in), group, and school (with subcategories, e.g., by curriculum/nationality) customer types, fully configurable to add further categories as needed.

The group/experience package builder lets the sales team assemble a package (admission, meals, workshops, etc.) against real-time inventory/resource availability and generate a quotation; revised quotations are tracked as successive versions if the customer negotiates, with configurable approval workflow for additional discounts.

- Once agreed, a quotation converts to a confirmed booking in the system — the same flow applies uniformly across groups, schools, and corporate customers.

- 4.8 Group Operations, Payment Links & Check-In

- An operations view shows upcoming group arrivals for the day/period and flags any deposits still required.

Group operational planning & tasks allow staff (e.g., a tour guide or educator) to be assigned to an incoming group ahead of arrival; participant/guest capture records individual group-member details where required.

Send Payment Link: the sales team can generate a payment link (e.g., for a deposit or full payment) that opens a B2C-style cart-review and checkout page reflecting the booking already created by the sales team. The link carries a configurable expiry (e.g., 24 hours, a week); if payment is not completed before expiry, the booking is automatically cancelled/released. This capability applies to any booking type — B2C, schools, corporates, or groups.

Fulfilment (ticket delivery via email/WhatsApp, reprint/resend options) and group arrival/check-in are tracked separately from ticket scanning — a dedicated group check-in status (arrived/checked-in vs. not yet arrived) helps operations manage dedicated group counters, distinct from the access-control scan that ultimately admits the group.

Group tickets support flexible QR configurations — a single QR code valid for a defined headcount, individual QR codes per member, or a single rotating/multi-use QR code.

- 4.9 Waiver / Consent Form Configuration

A dashboard tracks waiver form templates (published vs. draft) and completion status across customers. Templates can be cloned/duplicated and are built via drag-and-drop field configuration (name, DOB, custom fields, terms-and-conditions checkboxes).

Clarified: in response to Chinmay's question on a standard waiver template (akin to website white-labeling), Allam confirmed there is no single fixed standard — while a default/pre-set template can be offered, each business typically has its own specific waiver requirements, so the builder needs to remain fully configurable.

Dynamic field logic supports conditional questions (e.g., only ask for an Emirates city if the country selected is UAE; ask additional questions only if age is below a threshold). Signatory configuration defines who must sign (the participant or a parent/guardian); waiver-to-product association triggers the relevant waiver automatically when an associated product is purchased.

Confirmed: waiver trigger timing (at checkout, post-purchase, or on-site before entry) is business-configurable. Qossai noted that where a waiver is required before entry, access control should block entry until the waiver is completed — confirmed as supported (block ticket download, activation, check-in, or access if the waiver is incomplete).

Waiver versioning tracks template amendments over time; a mobile-optimized waiver view and an approval/testing/publication flow round out setup. Post-launch, a tracking dashboard shows per-participant completion status and delivery channel (email/WhatsApp/SMS), with minor/guardian handling and a verification workspace to check completeness and signatory validity, flagging missing, expired, or invalid waivers. Waivers can also be accessed via a QR code that opens the form directly.

- 4.10 Product Lifecycle, Catalog & Change Governance

The product lifecycle & catalog module (used by system administrators) tracks products from initial setup through approval to publish, with a dashboard of products by state (draft, pending approval, published) and a visual workflow (draft → approval → approved → scheduled → active).

Bulk product creation via template import/export, product ownership/assignment (department or team responsible for a product), channel publication controls, and a publish/activation scheduler (start/stop selling at defined times) were also covered, along with product duplication via a template library.

Product governance & change control: tracks all changes made to a published product (pricing, validity, etc.) with an approval workflow, review step, rollback/recovery, and version history.

Change impact analysis (raised by Chinmay): before a change is applied (e.g., to ticket validity), the system analyzes and surfaces which existing bookings, reservations, or promotions would be affected, alerting both admin and customer-facing teams before the change is confirmed.

Discussed (Chinmay): for higher-risk changes, it should be possible to apply the change only from a chosen future effective date, so the impact analysis and rollout can be managed deliberately rather than immediately — Allam agreed this aligns with how the system should behave.

Confirmed: changes to a product's price or configuration never retroactively affect tickets already purchased under the prior configuration — a guest who already bought at a given price keeps that price and terms regardless of later changes.

- 4.11 Sales Channel, Pricing & Inventory Allocation

Sales channels (onsite, B2C, B2B, kiosk, etc.) are configured and assigned per venue; products can then be made available on all channels or restricted to specific channels.

Confirmed: channel-specific pricing is required — e.g., online tickets are commonly priced lower than onsite/counter tickets in the region, reflecting reduced staff assistance for online purchases.

- Inventory can be centralized (shared across all channels) or split by percentage/quantity per channel (e.g., 50% online / 50% onsite).

Requested (Qossai): automatic inventory migration rules between channels — e.g., if B2C inventory sells out, the system should be able to automatically pull a configured share (e.g., 20%) from B2B inventory — confirmed this belongs in the same sales-channel/inventory configuration area.

Referenced an existing industry example (a competitor's pricing matrix tool) as a strong UX reference for configuring channel-and-variant pricing in a single matrix view (e.g., adult/child × onsite/online/kiosk); Qossai noted the goal is not to copy it exactly but to match or improve on it where a better approach is identified.

Sales schedule & validity: start/stop-sell timing is configurable per channel — e.g., some experiences (like a distant desert-safari tour) disallow same-day online booking (next-day minimum) since the platform can't assume the guest is already near the venue, whereas onsite sales generally remain open up to sell-out or a defined cutoff (e.g., 15 minutes before a timed show starts).

- 4.12 Resale Marketplace

A resale marketplace concept was introduced, allowing a guest who purchased a ticket to resell it to another customer through a secured channel, with a configurable commission and eligibility rules (e.g., minimum time before the ticket's validity/date, no reselling of expired tickets).

Open question raised (Allam/Qossai): whether this resale channel should be built and owned by TICVAI as a dedicated secure portal, or implemented within each client's own B2C website/app, given that the client (not TICVAI) legally owns and manages the underlying ticket. Qossai noted the motivation is to reduce ticket-resale fraud (e.g., guests copying and reselling the same ticket to multiple buyers) by offering a secure, TICVAI-controlled alternative to third-party resale sites.

Agreed: Chinmay (together with Dinesh) and Qossai will each separately research how major ticketing platforms handle secure resale and come back with a recommended approach — marked as pending confirmation from both sides.

- 4.13 UX Reference Walkthrough & Payment Gateway Approach

Allam walked through a live reference website (“Little Explorer,” a Dubai family-entertainment venue) as a UX benchmark: multi-location selector, a horizontal near-term date picker with a full calendar fallback, and tabbed browsing (passes/workshops/packages) all within a single page rather than multiple screens.

Highlighted details included: sibling/multi-buy discount pricing shown transparently with a struck-through original price; workshop add-ons presented inline with theme/cuisine sub-selection feeding directly into time-slot availability; a package builder for bundled experiences; and a date-change flow that detects conflicts across an existing multi-ticket cart and lets the guest shift the whole booking to a new date in one action.

At checkout, guests can sign in, register (with a visible loyalty-points incentive), or continue as guest; terms acceptance is implied by proceeding to payment rather than via a separate checkbox.

Payment gateway approach: the reference site embeds card/Apple Pay/Tabby payment capture directly on its own checkout page rather than redirecting to the payment gateway's hosted page. Allam explained both approaches should be supported — a standard redirect to the gateway's page, or an embedded/iframe-based capture that preserves the platform's own look and feel — noting that embedded capture requires additional security certification to reassure guests their card details are safely handled, and that this should be available for both Network International and Stripe integrations.

- Allam will share the reference website link with the team for further review.

- 4.14 Planning & Next Steps

- Remaining modules still to be covered include access control, promotions, cross-sell, the licensing module, IES, and device manager.

Agreed: sessions will continue daily at 8:30 AM (Allam's time) / 10:00 AM (Qossai's time), with the team aiming to complete all remaining workshop modules within roughly the next two weeks.

### 5. Key Decisions & Agreements

- Communications and notifications will be built as a single centralized module shared across all other modules, rather than per-module notification logic.

- Notification triggers must key off precise event states (e.g., ticket scanned/used) rather than the transaction alone, where the business intent requires it.

Published product/price changes never retroactively affect tickets already purchased under the prior configuration; change impact analysis will show affected bookings/reservations before a change is confirmed, with support for effective-dated changes on higher-risk updates.

- The group/school/corporate booking flow (inquiry → package builder → quotation → approval → confirmed booking) is unified across all these customer categories.

- “Send Payment Link” will be available across booking types (B2C, groups, schools, corporates), with configurable expiry and automatic cancellation of unpaid bookings after expiry.

- Group check-in will be tracked as a distinct operational status, separate from the access-control ticket scan that admits guests.

Waiver forms support fully configurable fields, conditional/dynamic logic, and configurable trigger timing (at purchase vs. on-site before entry), with incomplete waivers able to block ticket download, activation, check-in, or venue access.

Products must support channel-specific pricing (onsite, online, B2B, kiosk) and both centralized and split/percentage-based inventory allocation, with automatic overflow/migration rules between channels when one channel sells out.

- Both redirect-based and embedded/iframe-based payment capture will be supported for gateway integrations (Network International, Stripe), subject to the certification required for embedded capture.

### 6. Open Items / Questions for Follow-Up

- Resale marketplace ownership and approach (TICVAI-native secure portal vs. client-managed B2C channel) — pending research from both Chinmay/Dinesh and Qossai.

- Refinement of the effective-dated change-impact-analysis workflow — pending from the Softlabs team.

- Resale marketplace screen/documentation — pending from Allam.

### 7. Action Items

## 2026-09-01

`sources/mom/TICVAI_MoM_2026-09-01_Pricing_Upgrades_Media_Reservations_Resale.docx` · 3,307 words

### Minutes of Meeting

- Workshop — Pricing Engine, Upgrades, Media/Wallet Credentials, Reservations, Privacy & Resale Marketplace

### Date

- 01-September-2026

### Project

- TICVAI

### Meeting Type

- Product Workshop — Pricing, Upgrades, Media/Wallet Credentials, Reservations, Privacy & Resale Marketplace

### Prepared by

- Chitrangi Mestry

### Primary Objective

To walk through the pricing engine in full detail (structure, rules, taxes, governance, dynamic pricing and AI forecasting), followed by ticket upgrade configuration, media/credential and wallet setup, order and reservation management, privacy/consent and cookie handling, and a deeper follow-up on the resale marketplace approach introduced the previous day — alongside a parallel discussion on infrastructure sizing benchmarks.

### Participants

- TICVAI Team

- Softlabs Team

### Agenda

- Pricing foundation and structure — price lists, categories, rate types and rate structure

- Pricing rules — customer segment, membership, residency, channel and venue

- Volume/quantity-based pricing and loyalty points

- Seasonal and date-based pricing; pricing rule priority and hierarchy

- Taxes, fees and price calculation

- Price governance — approval, versioning, bulk updates and rollback

- Dynamic pricing strategies — seasonal, BOGO/sibling discounts, early-bird phased releases, inventory-based pricing

- AI demand forecasting and pricing simulation

- Ticket upgrade and downgrade configuration

- Media and credentials — QR, RFID, NFC, and Apple/Google Wallet

- Order and reservation management

- Amendment, cancellation and booking status

- Privacy consent and cookie policy

- Resale marketplace — detailed follow-up on approach and ticket ownership handling

- Infrastructure sizing and costing follow-up

- Planning for tomorrow's session (access control)

### 4. Detailed Discussion

- 4.1 Pricing Foundation & Structure

Allam introduced the pricing module across roughly seven sub-screens: an overview dashboard of all pricing setups and their status; the price list, which can be created per sales channel, segment, or product category (multiple price lists can coexist for different purposes); price category & rate type, which defines sub-groupings within a price list (e.g., adult, child, member); and rate structure, which sets the amount against a product category.

Rates and products are then associated to a price list (defining which categories/products/rates apply together); bundle pricing configures pricing for packages with multiple components (e.g., admission plus a meal) and any add-ons; and multi-market/currency pricing sets different prices and currencies by country, market, or venue.

A price hierarchy screen defines which pricing level takes precedence when multiple pricing levels could apply (category level, item level, segment level, etc.); a price-list cloning capability allows an existing price list (e.g., B2C) to be copied and adjusted (e.g., discounted for B2B) rather than rebuilt from scratch; and a final validation screen confirms the overall pricing setup is complete and ready to use.

- 4.2 Pricing Rules — Segment, Membership, Residency, Channel & Venue

- Pricing rules are configured on top of the price-list structure, with an overview screen showing all rules, their status, and any conflicts.

Rules can be defined by customer segment/profile (e.g., regular guest, school, corporate, group — consistent with the customer categories discussed the previous day), each with its own pricing.

- Membership pricing is treated as its own product type, with special prices and benefits configurable for members.

Rules also support residency/nationality/market-based pricing (e.g., UAE-resident vs. non-resident), channel-based pricing (onsite POS, B2C, kiosk, B2B each with independent pricing), and venue/event-level pricing (different pricing per venue, attraction, or specific event).

- 4.3 Volume/Quantity Pricing & Loyalty

Quantity-based pricing applies discounts based on group size or purchase volume — commonly used for groups and B2B partners, where tiered volume bands (e.g., up to 1,000 tickets at one rate, 1,000–5,000 at a better rate, above 5,000 at a further discount) apply automatically as sales volume increases.

- Regular customer purchase history is tracked against their profile, feeding a loyalty-points model where spend accumulates points that can later be redeemed.

- 4.4 Seasonal & Date-Based Pricing; Rule Priority

Seasonal pricing applies a different rate before/after a defined date (e.g., low-season summer pricing through 30 September, high-season pricing from 1 October); date-based pricing more generally allows a price change to apply to any purchase made on or after a specific date.

Raised (Chinmay): asked which rule takes precedence when multiple pricing rules could apply to the same sale simultaneously (e.g., a summer-season rate and a school-group discount on the same ticket) — whether one rule overrides the other, both apply together, or the system should default to whichever price is lowest.

Confirmed: conflicts are resolved via the configurable pricing hierarchy (introduced in 4.1) rather than an automatic “lowest price wins” default — the hierarchy determines which rule supersedes or overrides another when more than one could apply to the same sale.

Time-slot-based pricing allows prices to vary by show/session/time slot, since performances and time slots are associated to events, which in turn carry the event's pricing configuration; pricing rule priority governs which rule is ultimately applied within a single sale when conflicts exist.

- 4.5 Taxes, Fees & Price Calculation

- Taxes can be configured as inclusive or exclusive, and associated at the product or category level.

Fees are a distinct concept from taxes and can be defined flexibly — e.g., a convenience fee for call-center bookings, or a shipping fee that varies by destination (e.g., within Dubai vs. Abu Dhabi vs. Ras Al Khaimah vs. international), calculated automatically based on the address entered at checkout. Fees can be applied at the transaction, item, or ticket level.

- A tax profile groups the applicable taxes for a ticket/item, supporting multiple taxes calculated together, including tax-on-tax scenarios required in some countries (e.g., Egypt).

Confirmed (region-specific tax-on-discount handling): in some regions (e.g., Egypt), tax is calculated on the full pre-discount price rather than the discounted price — e.g., a AED 100 ticket with a 20% discount is paid at AED 80, but tax is still calculated on the AED 100 base. This inclusion/exclusion behavior must be configurable by region.

Confirmed: rounding precision must support regions requiring up to three decimal places, without rounding away the third decimal where the local currency requires exact figures.

- Tax exemption configuration allows specific products/transactions to be flagged so tax is not calculated at all where required.

- 4.6 Price Governance — Approval, Versioning, Bulk Updates & Rollback

Price changes go through an approval workflow before publishing, with full version control (e.g., a ticket priced at AED 100, revised to AED 110, then AED 120, tracked as versions 1.0, 1.1, 1.2) for every increase or decrease.

Bulk pricing updates (e.g., a flat percentage discount or price adjustment applied across all retail or F&B items at once) and bulk import of new items with their prices are both supported, alongside a rollback mechanism with full change history if a price update needs to be reversed.

- 4.7 Dynamic Pricing Strategies

Dynamic pricing covers several strategies: seasonal variation (as in 4.4); quantity-based promotions such as “buy 2, get the 3rd free” or buy-one-get-one (BOGO) offers; and tiered sibling-style discounts (first child at full price, subsequent children at a reduced rate) as discussed in a prior session.

Early-bird phased pricing (events): a new event can launch with an early-bird discount (e.g., 20% off a AED 200 base price) for a defined inventory quota (e.g., the first 200 of 500 tickets), followed by a second, smaller-discount phase (e.g., 10% off for the next 100 tickets), before reverting to full price for the remainder — both discount level and quota are configurable per phase.

Inventory/availability-based pricing: similar to airline-style dynamic pricing, price can increase (or decrease) automatically as available inventory/capacity is consumed — e.g., price steps up once a defined capacity threshold (such as 50% sold) is crossed, and again as availability becomes scarce.

- 4.8 AI Demand Forecasting & Pricing Simulation

AI-based demand forecasting can recommend pricing/promotional action ahead of anticipated demand shifts — e.g., forecasting an upcoming rain event and recommending a discount or promotion to sustain sales during a period when demand is expected to drop.

- A pricing simulation/test tool lets the business validate a proposed price change and preview its likely impact before applying it live.

- 4.9 Ticket Upgrade & Downgrade Configuration

- An upgrade dashboard shows upgrade/exchange volume and revenue generated from upgrades for a given period.

Upgrade/exchange rules define which products can be upgraded to which other products (e.g., an adult ticket to a membership, or a lower membership tier to a higher one), with downgrade paths also supported where the business allows it.

Upgrade eligibility: the system checks ticket validity/usage status before allowing an upgrade. Two illustrative use cases were discussed: upgrading a seated-event ticket to a better section on the same day (pay the difference at the counter), and upgrading a general-admission ticket to a season pass, where the amount already paid is credited toward the new product and only the balance is charged.

Clarified (Chinmay's question on upgrade windows): upgrade controls can restrict upgrades to before use, after use within a defined window, or up to a cut-off before the ticket/day ends — e.g., an event ticket may remain upgradeable until the guest exits, while a used day-ticket generally cannot be upgraded the following day.

Upgrade financial treatment — pro-rata calculation: for usage-based products like memberships, the system calculates a pro-rata credit based on how much of the original entitlement period has already been used (e.g., 2 months used out of a 1-year silver membership), and charges only the balance difference required to upgrade to the higher tier.

Upgrade rules can also apply at the product-attribute level (e.g., a child ticket sold based on height, later found to be an adult by height on arrival, upgraded to an adult ticket with the difference charged).

Bulk/group upgrade operations allow staff to upgrade multiple tickets in one action rather than one at a time; a distinct “quick upgrade” allows a direct, single-path upgrade (e.g., gold membership → platinum) versus a flexible upgrade where the guest can choose among several eligible target products.

Confirmed: upgrade functionality must be available on the guest-facing mobile/web app, not only at the venue counter — guests should be able to view eligible upgrade options and complete the upgrade online without visiting on-site.

Clarified (group upgrades): whether a group ticket can be upgraded is a business-configurable decision (via the conversion/eligibility rules) rather than enabled by default; where allowed, a group would typically raise an upgrade request (e.g., via chat/support) rather than self-service the upgrade the same way an individual guest would.

- 4.10 Media & Credentials (QR, RFID, NFC & Wallets)

A media is any identifier through which a ticket is presented/redeemed — QR code, RFID/wristband, facial recognition, or another form factor — fully configurable per business, whether or not it integrates with access control or handheld scanners.

Virtual tickets (generated but not physically printed) are configurable in terms of media ID format — prefix, suffix, and length — and multiple media types can be linked to a single ticket (e.g., a season pass usable via face recognition, QR code, or RFID as fallback options if one method is unavailable).

Wallet configuration (Apple Wallet / Google Wallet) covers template design — background color, header, footer — and the guest-facing “Add to Apple Wallet” flow after an online purchase.

Raised (Qossai): clarified that QR-code-based Apple/Google Wallet passes are straightforward to build, but NFC support inside a wallet pass may require direct engagement with Apple for certification/approval. He described an alternative: using an access-control vendor's (HID's) SDK to enable NFC-like functionality on a guest's phone without going through Apple directly, working with HID's own reader hardware.

Discussed (Chinmay): confirmed that a native Apple-certified NFC pass would work with any compatible reader, whereas the HID SDK-based approach would likely only work with HID's own readers — a meaningful compatibility trade-off. Chinmay will research how involved the direct-Apple-certification path is before committing to a direction, and lean toward that approach unless it proves to be a hard blocker, to avoid locking the platform into a single reader vendor.

- 4.11 Order & Reservation Management

The sales team can create bookings for any customer type (individual, school, corporate) and send a booking confirmation; on arrival, guests present the confirmation to collect physical media or scan directly at access control.

A dashboard shows total orders/reservations for the day, confirmed guests, and booking status; order details show the customer and the specific tickets/items in that order.

Reservation/hold policy configuration defines how long a capacity-based booking is held pending payment before it is released back to inventory if payment is not completed.

Booking status stages were outlined: draft → reserved (awaiting payment) → completed, with paths to cancelled or expired as applicable. Channel-specific rules govern what actions each channel can perform (create, upgrade, cancel), and whether checkout requires guest checkout (name, phone, email only) or full registration/sign-in.

Bookings can be linked to the appropriate customer category (corporate account, travel agent/B2B, school) which determines what additional information is collected. Order lines show the full contents of an order (tickets, retail, F&B) with associated inventory hold/availability; a final completeness check confirms payment, customer, and capacity requirements are all satisfied before an order is finalized. An upcoming/at-risk bookings view flags bookings nearing expiry (e.g., payment not yet completed) for follow-up.

- 4.12 Amendment, Cancellation & Booking Status

- Amendments and cancellations are checked against the applicable cancellation/amendment/reschedule policy before the system allows a refund, cancellation, or reschedule to proceed.

- A booking's overall financial status (deposit required, partial payment, full payment) is tracked centrally.

Confirmed (partial payments): partial payment/deposit is supported for bulk bookings such as schools and corporates — e.g., a 20–30% deposit upfront with the balance due on or before arrival.

- 4.13 Privacy Consent & Cookie Policy

Privacy consent capture during checkout covers marketing/newsletter opt-in and preferred contact method (email vs. phone), giving the marketing team a clear, compliant list of who can be contacted and how.

Cookie policy management supports a configurable consent banner (accept/reject) per website, with certain cookies flagged as mandatory (non-rejectable) and others optional, templated and configurable within the system.

- 4.14 Resale Marketplace — Detailed Follow-Up

Recap (Qossai): confirmed TICVAI's own resale engine will support three access models — (1) the client's own B2C website, where an end user requests to resell a ticket within an admin-configured resale price range (e.g., 10–20% below the original price); (2) a TICVAI-hosted white-label resale portal for clients without their own B2C presence (e.g., “museum.tickvai.com”); and (3) an API-based option for clients who run their own resale market but consume TICVAI's resale engine underneath.

Board 1 (resale rules) defines eligibility criteria, allowable resale price range, applicable fees/commission to the venue/tenant, and any required approval step. Board 2 covers what happens when a resale ticket is purchased — payment handling, ownership transfer, and settlement to the original seller.

Raised (Qossai): questioned whether reselling a ticket should cancel the original virtual ticket ID and issue a brand-new one, or instead keep the same virtual ID and simply change the owner/media linked to it.

Raised (Chinmay): cautioned that cancelling and reissuing a new ID on every resale could hurt reporting/traceability (e.g., tracking cancellations), drawing a parallel to finance ledgers, where records are never altered, only appended to preserve a full audit trail.

Decision: the original virtual ticket ID is preserved through a resale — only the owner name and associated media (e.g., the QR code) are changed, giving a complete, traceable ownership history against a single stable ID (e.g., ID VT0010: originally Qossai, resold to Allam, resold again to Chinmay). A separate ownership change-log table will track each transfer, so that reporting, finance, and other downstream services continue to operate against the same stable ID without needing to change how they reference tickets.

Board 3 covers the white-label resale page itself — how a guest lists a ticket for resale, sets a price within the allowed range, and how a buyer searches, browses, and receives the new ticket after purchase; the resale summary also shows the market fee TICVAI retains as revenue on each resale transaction. An active/sold/expired/pending resale-listing dashboard gives an overview of all resale activity.

Noted (Qossai): resale is expected to be used almost exclusively for event tickets (e.g., concerts, sports) rather than open-dated admission tickets, since admission tickets are generally flexible enough that resale demand is minimal.

- 4.15 Infrastructure Sizing & Costing Follow-Up

Requested (Chinmay): following up on last week's infrastructure/costing discussion, asked Qossai and Allam for concrete venue-scenario benchmarks — expected requests-per-second for events, and daily transaction volumes by venue type — to translate into a recommended AWS/GCP configuration and cost estimate, rather than working only from the earlier placeholder figures (e.g., 10,000 customers, 10 venues).

Clarified (Qossai): exact client-specific numbers can't be known in advance, but representative small/medium/large venue scenarios (e.g., a venue with around 1,000 daily visitors and 10 POS/access-control points, versus a 60,000-capacity stadium event) can be provided as planning estimates, with the understanding that actual client scale will vary and the system must be built to scale flexibly rather than sized for one fixed assumption.

Reiterated (Allam): as discussed previously with Dinesh, Softlabs should also propose the reverse view — e.g., how many transactions per hour or concurrent users a given infrastructure tier can support — so the two sides can align on a recommended minimum infrastructure configuration together.

- 4.16 Planning & Next Steps

- Tomorrow's session (same time, 8:30 AM) will be extended to roughly 1.5 hours to allow enough time to fully cover the access control module.

- Following access control, upcoming sessions will move to promotions and cross-sell.

### 5. Key Decisions & Agreements

- Conflicts between simultaneously applicable pricing rules are resolved via the configurable pricing hierarchy, not an automatic “lowest price wins” default.

- Tax-on-discount calculation behavior (full price vs. discounted price) and decimal/rounding precision (up to three decimal places in some regions) must both be region-configurable.

- Published price changes never retroactively affect tickets already purchased under a prior price/version.

- Membership and other usage-based upgrades use pro-rata calculation, crediting unused entitlement period toward the cost of the upgraded product.

- Upgrade functionality must be available across all channels, including the guest mobile/web app, not only on-site.

- Group ticket upgrades are business-configurable (not default-enabled) and are expected to be handled as a request (e.g., via chat/support) rather than guest self-service.

The resale marketplace preserves the original virtual ticket ID through a resale; only owner and media are changed, with a separate change-log table tracking ownership history for full traceability.

Resale will be supported via three access models: the client's own B2C site, a TICVAI-hosted white-label resale portal, and an API-based integration into a client's own resale market.

- Partial payment/deposit is supported for bulk (school/corporate) bookings, with the balance due on or before arrival.

### 6. Open Items / Questions for Follow-Up

- Documentation for the pricing engine, upgrade configuration, order/reservation management, and resale marketplace — pending from Allam.

- NFC/Apple Wallet integration approach (direct Apple certification vs. HID SDK-based NFC) — pending research from Chinmay.

- Venue-scenario benchmarks for infrastructure sizing (small/medium/large venue traffic estimates) — pending from Qossai/Allam, in consultation with Dinesh.

- Recommended infrastructure configuration and cost estimate based on those benchmarks — pending from Chinmay once the benchmark data is received.

### 7. Action Items

- Action Item

- Owner

- Share documentation for the pricing engine, upgrade configuration, order/reservation management, and resale marketplace covered today

- Allam
