## 2026-09-02

`sources/mom/TICVAI_MoM_2026-09-02_AccessControl.docx` · 3,134 words

### Minutes of Meeting

- Workshop — Access Control (Devices, Rules, Dynamic QR Code, Media/Credentials & Live Operations)

### Date

- 02-September-2026

### Project

- TICVAI

### Meeting Type

- Product Workshop — Access Control (Devices, Rules, Dynamic QR, Media/Credentials & Live Operations)

### Prepared by

- Chitrangi Mestry

### Primary Objective

To walk through the access control module in full detail across its ~12 configuration boards — device/gate management, access rules and entitlements, dynamic QR code design, media and credential handling, facial recognition, turnstile hardware, offline synchronization, and live operations — as an extended session ahead of moving on to promotions and cross-sell.

### Participants

- TICVAI Team

- Softlabs Team

### Agenda

- Access control overview — venue/gate visualization and device management

- Device integration architecture, health monitoring and alerts

- Access rules — entry/exit, anti-passback and validity

- Multi-park crossover, companion rules and group admission

- Rule simulation tool

- Dynamic QR code — concept, generation approach and offline requirement

- Dynamic QR code — business flexibility and exceptions

- Device binding, credential transfer and revocation

- Media and credential configuration

- Facial recognition — Face Pass, Face Tag and enrollment

- Privacy and biometric data retention

- Media as a payment method

- Turnstile hardware and handheld scanner configuration

- Offline mode and synchronization

- Guest journey, group/B2B profiles and live operations dashboard

- Ticket lookup, manual override, dynamic/attribute-based access control and fraud detection

- Planning for tomorrow's session (promotions and cross-sell)

### 4. Detailed Discussion

- 4.1 Access Control Overview & Gate/Device Visualization

Allam introduced a venue-wide attendance overview (open/closed gates, offline/maintenance status, graphed) and a visual map of all access control locations across multiple venues/tenants, including entry and exit turnstile layouts that vary by venue.

Gate and zone management shows how many physical gates exist per location (e.g., three gates at a “main entry plaza,” two at a “main entry zone”); a device inventory view lists all access control devices (turnstiles and handheld scanners) that can be added and assigned per gate.

Devices are added to the system by selecting an integrated turnstile model and configuring its connection details (e.g., IP address); a real-time health-check view shows device connectivity status across the estate.

- 4.2 Device Integration Architecture, Health Monitoring & Alerts

Confirmed (Qossai): integration happens at two levels — the turnstile itself and the reader — each producing its own outputs. Devices push events to TICVAI via a TCP/IP API (confirmed with a turnstile vendor during the session): anti-passback attempts, power loss, network loss, and other fault conditions are detected by the device itself and sent to TICVAI as alarms/events, rather than requiring TICVAI to poll or independently detect hardware state.

Confirmed: TICVAI's role is to receive these vendor-pushed events and surface them as alerts/reports (e.g., notifying the operations team automatically when a turnstile goes offline) rather than to build fault-detection logic itself.

An example of extended integration was also raised: some turnstile vendors can trigger a linked CCTV system to capture footage on an anti-passback attempt, which can then be emailed to security — the turnstile is generally treated as the primary integration point, but the reader supplies its own outputs where the turnstile alone doesn't.

- 4.3 Access Rules — Entry/Exit, Anti-Passback & Validity

An access rules dashboard shows active rules, drafts, and status; rules define validity conditions (e.g., valid for a single day, a week) and are configured by an administrator based on business need.

Entry/exit rules cover: one entry per day vs. unlimited or limited re-entry; whether an exit scan is required, or whether exit turnstiles are left in free-rotation with headcount inferred from passage; and configurable turnstile modes (free rotation, entry, exit).

Anti-passback rules prevent a scanned ticket from being scanned again within a configured time window, with an "exit-before-re-entry" option to prevent a ticket being passed back out to let another person in.

Discussed (edge case — scan without physical passage): Chinmay raised the risk of a guest scanning a ticket but not physically passing through the turnstile (e.g., due to a stroller or a brief delay causing the turnstile to re-lock), then being unable to re-scan since the system already marked the ticket as used.

Decision: the system will treat a successful scan as “used” regardless of physical passage, to close off a fraud vector; genuine cases are resolved manually by security via the ticket's scan-history log rather than by loosening the used/unused rule — confirmed by both Allam and Qossai as the safer approach.

Validity and calendar rules define the date range a ticket is valid for, plus configurable blockout dates (e.g., certain tickets excluded from use on public holidays or special event days); an entitlement consumption engine tracks how many entries a ticket has used against its allowance and blocks further use once exhausted.

- 4.4 Multi-Park Crossover, Companion Rules & Group Admission

Multi-park crossover rules (for multi-venue/multi-tenant operators) define how many different parks a multi-day ticket can be used at, whether multiple parks can be visited in the same day or are limited to one per day, and whether usage days must be consecutive from first scan or can be used flexibly within a longer validity window.

Companion rules can require a dependent ticket type (e.g., a child ticket) to be accompanied by a qualifying ticket (e.g., an adult) to gain entry.

Group admission supports multiple models: a single media scanned once to admit an entire counted group; a single QR code that can be scanned repeatedly (rotating admission) until the group's headcount is exhausted; or multiple individual QR codes for a group, scanned independently over time.

- 4.5 Rule Simulation Tool

A simulation/test tool allows an administrator to validate a configured access rule (e.g., a ticket permitted in Zone A and B but not C or D) via a virtual scan before publishing, without needing to run a real transaction.

- 4.6 Dynamic QR Code — Concept, Generation Approach & Offline Requirement

Dynamic QR codes refresh periodically (rather than remaining static) to reduce fraud/resale risk, and typically require additional hardware (beacons) at the venue in addition to turnstiles.

Two generation approaches discussed (Qossai): (1) beacon-based — the QR code stays hidden until the guest's phone is detected near a gate-mounted beacon via Bluetooth, at which point the code is generated and refreshes every ~2 minutes; and (2) app-generated — the mobile app itself generates the refreshing code without beacon proximity detection. Qossai noted beacon-based is generally considered more secure, since the dynamic code isn't simply stored/derivable on the device itself.

Hard requirement raised (Qossai): the dynamic QR code must still be able to appear and function without an active internet connection, since large, crowded events (e.g., 10,000+ attendees) commonly experience severe network congestion. Whatever generation approach is chosen must work offline via Bluetooth/beacon proximity or an equivalent local mechanism.

Discussed (Chinmay): raised GPS geofencing as a possible complementary/simpler approach, and flagged a technical limitation of Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) beacons — a single BLE connection point generally serves one device at a time, which could complicate simultaneous detection for a queue of multiple guests. Qossai noted that in a prior real-world deployment, adjustable BLE signal range (e.g., 1–2 meters) successfully handled this by ensuring only the nearest guest's device would trigger, with the resulting QR code valid across any turnstile in that gate zone.

Action: Qossai to share (has already shared via WhatsApp) a scope-of-work / reference document from a prior real-world dynamic QR code deployment for the team's review.

The QR code's payload/definition must embed identifying components (e.g., ticket ID) so that, even offline, a reader can cryptographically validate that a scanned code was genuinely generated by the TICVAI platform rather than accept or reject based on connectivity alone.

Credential activation and display rules control when a dynamic QR code becomes visible (e.g., blurred until beacon proximity is detected, then activated and refreshing on a short interval, such as every 6–12 seconds) and prevent screenshot capture of the active code.

- 4.7 Dynamic QR Code — Business Flexibility & Exceptions

- Raised (Chinmay): asked how physical, on-site POS-issued tickets fit into a fully dynamic-QR event, since those are generated and used same-day at the venue.

Clarified (Qossai/Allam): a venue decides upfront, per event, whether it will be sold entirely via dynamic QR code or allow normal tickets — for a fully dynamic event, even POS-purchased tickets are delivered by email/SMS with instructions to download the app and link the ticket, rather than issued as a static QR code on the spot. The system must support both modes and mixed configurations, since dynamic QR is primarily valuable for high-fraud-risk, high-demand ticketed events (concerts, sports, capacity-constrained shows) rather than general admission (e.g., museums), where resale/fraud risk is minimal.

Flagged as an open exception (Qossai): VIP/premium invitations (physically delivered passes) and B2B/reseller-issued tickets don't cleanly fit a fully-dynamic-QR-only policy and may need to fall back to a standard QR code or RFID card — confirmed the platform should support a per-product override to disable dynamic QR for specific ticket types as an exception, even within an otherwise fully-dynamic event.

Confirmed (Pradnya's question): any ticket purchased online for a dynamic-QR event must be linked to the mobile app to display the working code — web/desktop purchases are redirected into the app experience for activation, not exempted from it.

- 4.8 Device Binding, Credential Transfer & Revocation

Device binding maps a digital ticket to a single approved device ID once activated in the app, preventing the same login/ticket from being actively used by multiple people simultaneously on different devices; re-registering to a new device requires deactivating the prior binding.

Credential transfer allows a guest who can no longer attend to formally transfer their ticket to another person's device, after which the original holder's copy is invalidated.

- Credential revocation automatically invalidates the prior ticket/credential whenever a refund, exchange, or reissue occurs.

Offline cryptographic validation (recap) allows gates to validate a QR code's authenticity locally when connectivity is down, synchronizing with the central system once back online.

- 4.9 Media & Credential Configuration

A media-types board defines all supported credential types (QR code, RFID, NFC, facial/biometric, etc.) and how each is supported and associated with a ticket — a ticket can carry a single media type or multiple in parallel.

Verification method configuration defines how a given ticket is validated at the gate (QR scan, facial match, RFID read); media issuance/encoding profile configuration defines what unique information is embedded in the credential (recapping the QR code definition/components discussed in 4.6).

Media swap: a zero-value transaction that converts a purchased ticket's media from one form to another on-site (e.g., scanning an online QR code at a kiosk to issue a physical wristband instead).

External partner ticket support: the system must be able to import and validate tickets issued by an approved reseller/partner platform through access control, even though those tickets originate outside TICVAI's own sales flow.

Hotel/PMS integration (recap): guests staying at an affiliated hotel can be issued a zero-value ticket/wristband after a room-number lookup and identity verification, or can charge on-site purchases (e.g., an activity) directly to their room via the same lookup — requiring integration with a property management system such as Opera, including vendor-provided certification of the integration.

- A media compatibility testing capability validates that each supported media type works correctly at each gate/device before go-live.

- 4.10 Facial Recognition — Face Pass, Face Tag & Enrollment

Two facial-recognition credential types confirmed: “Face Pass” — a permanent-style enrollment typically used for memberships/season passes, retained long-term and renewable; and “Face Tag” — a short-lived enrollment for a single-day or single-event ticket, not intended for long-term retention.

Enrollment can happen through multiple channels: the mobile app, the website, at the point of sale, via a self-service kiosk, or directly at the turnstile itself (scan the ticket, then look at the reader to enroll on first use) — covering guests who purchased through a channel without built-in enrollment (e.g., a B2B/reseller ticket).

- Re-enrollment/replacement and fallback-to-alternate-media (e.g., QR/RFID) are both supported if facial recognition fails to read at the gate.

- 4.11 Privacy & Biometric Data Retention

Raised (Chinmay): asked specifically about data-retention policy for facial recognition and other guest data — how long different data types should be kept, and any regional requirements.

Clarified (Allam): retention is business/venue-configurable rather than fixed by the platform; short-lived Face Tag data does not need retention beyond the visit, while Face Pass data tied to a membership/season pass needs to persist across renewal cycles.

Action (Qossai): recommended the team review the live consumer app and published privacy policy of an existing major venue-group client as a real-world reference for how facial-recognition consent, data use, and retention are explained to guests — to be used as a model for TICVAI's own privacy/consent design.

Broader context shared (Qossai): facial recognition adoption is expected to keep growing industry-wide as a convenience-driven guest experience improvement, reinforcing the importance of building it securely and transparently from the outset.

- 4.12 Media as a Payment Method

Beyond admission, the same media (wristband or enrolled face) can function as a stored-value payment method — e.g., a guest loads funds onto a wristband or their profile and pays for food, beverage, or retail by presenting the same credential, with balance checked and deducted automatically at the point of sale; top-up can similarly be completed via the same credential.

- 4.13 Turnstile Hardware & Handheld Scanner Configuration

Turnstile hardware configuration covers device connection details (e.g., IP address) plus supported light and sound feedback — for example, showing a green light for an adult ticket scan versus orange for a child ticket, giving on-site staff a quick visual fraud check if an adult attempts to use a child ticket. Some turnstile models also support audio (including celebratory sounds, e.g., for a birthday visit).

- Guest feedback/messaging design allows a custom welcome message and venue branding/logo to display on the reader on a successful scan.

Handheld scanner configuration covers standalone scanning devices that can read QR, RFID, or other supported media, alongside the broader software configuration and compatibility testing/deployment process for all access devices.

- 4.14 Offline Mode & Synchronization

When a device loses connectivity, it continues to validate tickets locally against the components embedded in the credential (recapping 4.6/4.8), queues the resulting transactions, and automatically synchronizes them back to the central access control system once connectivity is restored.

- 4.15 Guest Journey, Group/B2B Profiles & Live Operations Dashboard

A group/B2B admission profile view shows entry statistics by category — general admission, group admission, re-entry, and crossover — along with attendance breakdowns for schools and other group bookings based on scanned tickets.

The live operations dashboard shows real-time attendance by venue and by gate, including each gate's online/offline status and entry count. Turnstile mode (entry vs. exit) can be reconfigured through the day — e.g., more gates set to entry in the morning, shifted toward exit in the evening as visitors leave.

- 4.16 Ticket Lookup, Manual Override, Attribute-Based Access Control & Fraud Detection

A ticket/credential lookup view shows the complete scan history for any ticket — purchaser, gate, and timestamp for every scan attempt — supporting investigation of disputed or suspicious usage.

Manual override allows security staff to admit a guest despite a scan issue (e.g., a valid ticket that failed to register properly), with every override logged against that visitor's record for audit purposes.

Dynamic/attribute-based access control (ABAC): access decisions can consider who is scanning, what ticket type, where, when, and broader context — for example, denying entry to an otherwise valid, unused ticket once a venue's configured maximum live occupancy threshold is reached, until capacity frees up as other guests exit.

A fraud assessment view flags suspicious ticket usage patterns or potential security threats; a live monitoring view shows current attendance, in-park counts, and entry/exit/crossover activity per venue in real time.

- 4.17 Planning & Next Steps

- Tomorrow's session will move on to promotions and cross-sell, scheduled for 9:30 AM Dubai time (10:00 AM Qossai's time / 11:00 AM Chinmay's time).

- Allam to share the full access control documentation, along with outstanding documentation promised from the previous (pricing/resale) session.

### 5. Key Decisions & Agreements

Turnstile/reader fault and security events (offline, power loss, anti-passback attempt) are pushed to TICVAI by the vendor's API rather than independently detected by TICVAI — TICVAI's role is to receive, alert on, and report these events.

A successful ticket scan is always treated as “used,” regardless of whether the guest physically passed through the turnstile; edge cases are resolved manually by security via scan-history lookup rather than by relaxing this rule.

- Dynamic QR codes must remain functional without an active internet connection, given severe network congestion typical of large, crowded events.

Dynamic QR code enforcement is configurable per event/product — not a single platform-wide mode — with support for exceptions (VIP invitations, certain B2B/reseller flows, low-fraud-risk ticket types) to fall back to standard QR/RFID credentials.

The ticket is always a single virtual record in the backend; QR, RFID, NFC, facial recognition, and future credentials (e.g., hotel room key, city transit card) are interchangeable “media” linked to that same virtual ticket.

Facial recognition data will be managed under two distinct retention tiers — short-lived “Face Tag” for single-visit tickets and longer-retained “Face Pass” for memberships/season passes — configurable by business/venue.

Access control will support attribute-based, context-aware decisions, including venue-wide live capacity thresholds that can deny entry to an otherwise valid ticket when the venue is full.

### 6. Open Items / Questions for Follow-Up

- Recommended dynamic QR code generation approach (beacon/BLE-based vs. app-generated vs. hybrid, with reliable offline support) — pending research and proposal from Chinmay.

- Handling of B2B/reseller-issued tickets under a fully-dynamic-QR event policy — flagged as an unresolved edge case by Qossai.

- Facial recognition data retention periods and regional compliance requirements — to be defined referencing an existing client's live privacy policy.

- Full access control documentation (all boards) and outstanding pricing/resale documentation — pending from Allam.

### 7. Action Items

- Action Item

- Owner

- Status

- Share the full access control module documentation (all boards covered today), plus outstanding documentation promised from the previous pricing/resale session

- Allam

### 8. Next Steps

- Tomorrow's session (9:30 AM Dubai time) will cover promotions and cross-sell.

## 2026-09-07

`sources/mom/TICVAI_MoM_2026-09-07_Accreditation_Entitlements_VirtualQueue.docx` · 3,454 words

### Minutes of Meeting

- Workshop — Accreditation, Entitlements Portfolio Management & Virtual Queue

### Date

- 07-September-2026

### Project

- TICVAI

### Meeting Type

- Product Workshop — Accreditation, Entitlements Portfolio & Virtual Queue

### Prepared by

- Chitrangi Mestry

### Primary Objective

To walk through three modules — accreditation (registration, approval and credentialing for event/venue access), entitlements portfolio management (what a customer owns, can use and can transfer), and virtual queue (ride/attraction queue planning and allocation across walk-in, virtual-queue and VIP guests) — and to review an early prototype of the guest booking flow across multiple product categories.

### Participants

- TICVAI Team

- Softlabs Team

### Agenda

- Accreditation overview and application directory

- Accreditation form builder, categories and program setup

- Application requirements, document validation and OCR auto-fill

- Accreditation profile, identity verification and duplicate prevention

- Approval workflow, SLA and escalations

- Credential issuance, access rights and lifecycle management

- Notifications, bulk operations and analytics

- Accreditation channel placement (portal vs. mobile app) and API access

- Entitlements portfolio — structure, family/group and assignment

- Entitlements lifecycle, consumption monitoring and screen consolidation

- Entitlements usage, upgrades and refund/credit recovery

- Virtual queue — concept and lane/allocation model

- Virtual queue — mobile journey and configuration

- Virtual queue — multi-venue applicability (theme park vs. water park)

- Virtual queue — three-tier guest model and value preservation

- Virtual queue — wait-time calculation and people-counting technology

- Virtual queue — operations dashboard and AI guest flow optimization

- Guest booking flow prototype walkthrough

- Planning for upcoming sessions

### 4. Detailed Discussion

- 4.1 Accreditation Overview & Application Directory

Allam introduced accreditation as a registration and credentialing process for event/program access — participants submit required information through a customizable form, it goes through an approval process (including any required documents), and once approved they receive a badge/credential (photo badge, QR code, or RFID) used to access the event.

- An accreditation center dashboard summarizes all registrations — total registered, pending review, and expired documents — as an overview of approvals and activations.

- An application directory lets staff search and find accreditation applications by name, company, or other submitted business information.

- 4.2 Accreditation Form Builder, Categories & Program Setup

A new accreditation application flow allows a venue to create an account for a partner/company (main account or sub-accounts), who then log in and submit accreditation requests for their own members; entry can be done by the end user themselves or on their behalf by the admin team.

- The accreditation form builder allows drag-and-drop customization of exactly which fields are collected per form, before validation, approval and publishing.

- Accreditation category management supports different form/field sets per category — e.g., media, corporate, or individual guest — each with its own associated form.

- Accreditation program setup associates a given accreditation category to a specific event, venue, or season.

- Application type configuration defines category-specific requirements (e.g., contractors must provide company authorization), with a requirement matrix specifying exactly which documents each category must submit.

- 4.3 Application Requirements, Document Validation & OCR Auto-Fill

Submission tracking shows applications submitted, pending, and missing required documents; the system validates supported document types and formats (PDF, JPEG, PNG) and enforces file-size/quality limits at upload to avoid downstream issues.

Raised (Allam): asked whether uploading an ID document (e.g., Emirates ID, as an image or PDF) could automatically extract and populate the relevant form fields (ID number, expiry date, etc.) rather than requiring manual entry.

Confirmed (Chinmay): feasible via OCR — the system can read the uploaded ID/document image or PDF and auto-populate the corresponding fields. The extracted data must still be stored as structured fields (not just the image) so the system can track document expiry and prompt renewal ahead of an event.

Distinguished from passport scanning (Chinmay's reference to a prior client implementation): dedicated passport scanner hardware (as used in hotels) reads a passport directly via its own SDK, whereas accreditation document upload is typically a photo/PDF uploaded from a phone or laptop with no dedicated scanning hardware — the system needs to read and structure the data from that uploaded file instead.

- 4.4 Accreditation Profile, Identity Verification & Duplicate Prevention

An accreditation profile/identity management directory lets staff open a submitted application, review the photo and all entered details, and verify submitted documents are correct, legible and valid.

Confirmed: the system must validate uniqueness of key identifiers (e.g., passport number, Emirates ID) and block a duplicate submission, prompting the applicant to resolve or resubmit rather than silently creating a duplicate record.

Accreditation holders are linked to an organization/company profile; a main account holder (company/agent) can see the status of every accreditation application submitted under their organization — approved, rejected, or requiring resubmission — whether the end applicant collects the credential physically or receives a soft copy by email.

- 4.5 Approval Workflow, SLA & Escalations

Multi-level approval workflows are configurable by category — e.g., a government accreditation can follow a different approval chain than a private/corporate/media accreditation, each with its own reviewers and approvers.

SLA configuration sets a target turnaround (e.g., approve/reject within X days) per category, with alerts raised as volume builds up against that SLA (e.g., a backlog of pending media passes).

- Escalation rules automatically route an application to the next approval level if it remains unactioned beyond a configured point.

- 4.6 Credential Issuance, Access Rights & Lifecycle Management

Once approved, a credential/badge is issued — photo badge printing, QR code, or RFID — depending on what media types are supported and configured for that event; the credential can be collected physically or delivered digitally (e.g., to a mobile device) for scanning at access control.

Access rights define which zones a given accreditation category may enter (e.g., media may access all zones; a corporate accreditation may be limited to specific zones), enforced at the point of scan/check.

Accreditation lifecycle management covers the period from activation through expiry, renewal, or suspension — including the scenario where a submitted document (e.g., Emirates ID) expires before the event date, triggering a resubmission request and, if unresolved, a block on that credential.

- 4.7 Notifications, Bulk Operations & Analytics

- Applicants are notified at each status change — approved, rejected, or requiring further validation.

Bulk operations: a company with a large number of members (e.g., 1,000) can be provided an Excel template to submit all member details and documents at once, rather than registering one by one; once imported, each record still proceeds through profile selection, document submission, and approval.

Analytics and reporting show approvals, upcoming expiries, and per-portfolio/category detail, including attendance-vs-issued comparisons (e.g., 1,000 passes issued, 700 scanned as attended) and year-over-year or venue-over-venue comparisons of accreditation usage.

- 4.8 Accreditation Channel Placement & API Access

Raised (Chinmay): asked whether accreditation should be handled only via the guest web portal, or also built into the guest mobile app, given the configuration involves document uploads typically done from a proper web interface.

Clarified (Allam): accreditation is normally completed via the web portal, since it involves document upload and photo checks best suited to a larger screen; the same submission functionality should still be available on the mobile app as a secondary option for individuals who need it, but the portal remains the primary channel.

An accreditation API allows an external partner to build their own accreditation front end while consuming TICVAI's accreditation platform underneath, for organizations that prefer not to use TICVAI's own portal directly.

- 4.9 Entitlements Portfolio — Structure, Family/Group & Assignment

A central entitlements dashboard shows customers, families, corporates, and schools together with what tickets/benefits/entitlements each holds — usable both by the guest themselves (e.g., in the mobile app) and by customer service handling an inquiry (e.g., checking an annual pass issue).

- The portfolio structure/profile view shows a given customer's full entitlement picture — restrictions, wallet balance, and all associated entitlements in one place.

Family and dependent views show a family ticket's composition (e.g., two adults, two children) with the specific entitlements tied to each dependent; equivalent views exist for school and corporate bookings.

A unified/consolidated entitlement list shows everything a customer holds across a visit — e.g., four admission tickets, two fast passes, a meal package, and a parking entitlement — in one place.

The entitlement assignment manager defines who can receive and use an entitlement (e.g., the reservation owner holding all tickets on their profile, each with its own product-driven entitlement).

Ownership and transfer: a purchased ticket can be transferred to another guest (e.g., a friend) if the original buyer can no longer attend, with the system retaining a full record of the original purchaser and the transfer history.

Permissions and spending controls (recap from the wallet module) and credential/media association (linking a ticket to its media) both apply within the entitlements portfolio as well; a portfolio 360 view consolidates all of this per customer.

- 4.10 Entitlements Lifecycle, Consumption Monitoring & Screen Consolidation

A lifecycle/analytics view shows entitlements nearing expiry, and status breakdowns — active, reserved, consumed, transferred, expired, refunded/cancelled — as a ticket moves from purchase (active/reserved, holding inventory) through scan (consumed) or transfer, refund, cancellation, or expiry.

- A real-time consumption monitor shows how much of each customer's entitlement has been redeemed/used.

Raised (Chinmay): questioned whether this needed to be a separate monitoring page/platform distinct from the general entitlement monitoring already used for regular (non-accredited) guests, or whether accreditation-holder monitoring could instead be a filtered view within the same unified monitoring platform — to make it easy to quickly distinguish and support large accredited groups from general guests without maintaining a fully separate system.

Agreed (Allam): supportive of consolidating wherever the same information can reasonably be shown together — the priority is minimizing the number of separate screens an end user needs to navigate to find relevant information, rather than the number of underlying boards used to explain the concept during workshops.

- 4.11 Entitlements Usage, Upgrades & Refund/Credit Recovery

- Usage tracking (recap) reflects the entitlement configuration set per ticket — allowed usage count, re-entries allowed, etc., as covered in the ticketing configuration sessions.

- Upgrade mechanisms (recap) apply here as well — whether a given ticket has been upgraded is visible from the entitlements view.

Refund and credit value recovery follow the same refund-policy-driven process covered in the payment session — refund requests are approved through the operations/finance workflow, and the refunded value can go back to the original payment method or be credited to the guest's wallet for future purchases.

- 4.12 Virtual Queue — Concept & Lane/Allocation Model

Virtual queue applies mainly to theme parks/water parks with multiple rides. Guests typically hold either a general admission ticket or an express/fast-lane ticket (paid upgrade), with the venue running separate physical lanes for each at every ride.

Purpose: virtual queue helps a guest plan their day across many rides without physically standing in every line, so they don't end up completing only a couple of rides due to poor time management.

Allocation model: per-ride hourly capacity (e.g., 600 guests/hour, i.e., 10/minute) is split across three guest types — express/fast-lane, virtual queue, and physically-queuing walk-in guests (e.g., an illustrative 75% general capacity split between walk-in and virtual queue, 25%/150 guests for express) — and this allocation must adjust dynamically if one lane is disproportionately busy, rather than staying fixed.

- 4.13 Virtual Queue — Mobile Journey & Configuration

In the mobile app, a guest with a valid ticket can browse all rides, select one, and see the current wait time (e.g., 60 minutes); joining the virtual queue reserves a spot for their party and returns an estimated return window (e.g., 4:50–5:00 PM) based on current queue conditions.

- If a guest doesn't return within their allotted window, their reserved slot can be automatically released back into the queue for other guests.

Virtual queue configuration covers: which rides are enabled/disabled on a given day; the queue/express split allocation (as in 4.12); queue rules such as target wait time and return-window duration; and handling of early or late arrivals at the ride's entry scanner (a check-in point before entering the lane).

- 4.14 Virtual Queue — Multi-Venue Applicability (Theme Park vs. Water Park)

Raised (Allam): flagged that the smartphone-based virtual queue journey works well for theme parks, but water park guests typically don't carry their phones (often stored in lockers), so an alternative is needed.

Proposed approach: a kiosk at the ride/attraction where a guest scans their wristband to book a queue slot, receiving a return time without needing a smartphone — they return at the assigned time and scan their wristband to enter.

- 4.15 Virtual Queue — Three-Tier Guest Model & Value Preservation

Detailed input (Qossai): walked through the three distinct guest types at a ride — walk-in (physical line), virtual queue (booked via app/kiosk), and VIP (paid fast-lane) — and stressed these must be operationally distinguished at the ride itself.

Key concern: virtual queue guests must not be merged into the same physical line as VIP guests, since VIP guests pay specifically to minimize their wait and enter within minutes of arriving — mixing the two would erode the VIP guest's paid value. A virtual queue guest, while not waiting in a physical line, has still effectively “waited” (e.g., 60 minutes) before their return window, so the operational model needs its own dedicated handling at the ride (e.g., a separate line, or scanning a QR code within a specific arrival window) distinct from both VIP and walk-in guests.

Waiting-time honesty & recalculation: the return-time estimate given to a virtual queue guest must be genuinely accurate and should recalculate dynamically based on real-time conditions across all three guest tiers, not a static estimate.

- 4.16 Virtual Queue — Wait-Time Calculation & People-Counting Technology

Raised (Qossai): asked how actual per-ride occupancy/wait time would be calculated in practice — via entry sensors, manual security counts, or CCTV-based counting — since accurate real-time counts are essential to produce a reliable wait-time and return-window estimate for every guest tier.

Discussed (Chinmay): raised and then set aside GPS/device-clustering-based crowd estimation (inspired by tools like Google Maps) as likely too imprecise in small, dense areas; favored either existing line-monitoring sensors or computer-vision/CCTV-based people counting as more practical and already-proven approaches, cautioning against over-engineering beyond what's needed.

Agreed direction (Qossai): the specific technology/vendor is secondary to achieving an accurate per-ride count, however it's implemented (sensor, camera/CCTV, or manual); requested Allam check with an existing large-scale operator (Warner Bros. World was cited, which has a visible wait-time display) to understand what counting technology they use as a real-world reference before committing to an approach.

- 4.17 Virtual Queue — Operations Dashboard & AI Guest Flow Optimization

An operations view shows current wait time per ride (including separate general and virtual-queue wait times) with alerts for conditions like a growing express queue or unusually high overall queue length.

AI guest flow optimization: a visual venue map highlights rides with long queues versus low-queue alternatives, letting operations proactively redirect guests (e.g., a notification suggesting a nearby ride with a shorter wait) to spread demand and improve overall guest experience and ride throughput.

Revenue lever: the system should also proactively upsell an express/fast-lane ticket to a guest facing a long wait (e.g., “buy express ticket for [amount]”), balancing guest experience improvements with additional venue revenue.

- 4.18 Guest Booking Flow Prototype Walkthrough

Aishwarya demonstrated an in-progress desktop prototype of the guest ticket-booking platform, covering categories including events, movies, theme park, cabanas, attractions, activities, dining, resources, merchandise, and F&B.

Events: walked through a concert (seat-map selection modeled on the Coca-Cola Arena reference shared earlier, similar to Platinum List), a multi-day festival with day/time-slot selection, and a tiered-ticket show (early bird, couple, group-of-4, group-of-6 categories) — each following a similar add-to-cart and checkout flow.

- Movies: language/screen-type selection (e.g., English, Dolby Atmos), cinema and showtime selection, seat selection, and concession add-ons before checkout.

Theme park: ticket-type list (single-day, water park only, all-activities combo, annual pass, combo with F&B, etc.), guest-category breakdown (adult/child/senior/infant/people-of-determination with companion), and per-ticket guest-name capture driven by the selected ticket quantity.

Raised (Allam): asked whether a mobile version of these wireframes exists, noting most guests will book from a smartphone rather than desktop, making the mobile experience the higher priority to validate.

- Confirmed (Aishwarya): mobile wireframes are in progress and will be shared shortly.

Cabanas: category selection (premium, VIP, luxury, private, family, couples — modeled on existing Dubai cabana operators), date/time and guest-count selection, and amenity details before confirmation.

Activities: desert safari-style package selection (e.g., buy-one-get-one, evening safari, Bedouin-style safari), pickup-point and add-on (stroller) options, and duration-based packages (e.g., 2-hour/4-hour) for kids and sports activities, each following the same cart/checkout pattern.

Dining: two flows — book a table (date, time, group size, seating-area preference, occasion, allergy/special-request notes) and order food (delivery or pickup-location selection, item selection, checkout).

- Raised (Qossai): for table booking, whether the guest should choose a specific table.

Clarified (Allam): specific-table selection can be offered as an option, but the default/typical flow is the guest specifies party size and the system/host allocates an available table internally, rather than requiring the guest to pick one.

- Resources: a meeting-room booking flow (headcount, duration, time-slot, room selection, add-ons such as tea/coffee/snacks) modeled on the House of Wisdom reference shared previously.

- Merchandise: an e-commerce-style flow — product browsing, cart, pickup location or doorstep delivery, and checkout, including add/remove quantity controls.

- F&B (final flow shown): outlet and menu browsing, item selection, and delivery/pickup options (collect at counter, curbside pickup, doorstep delivery, priority delivery) before checkout.

Wrap-up: Qossai and Allam asked Aishwarya to share the prototype link so they can review it independently and schedule a separate feedback call once reviewed.

### 5. Key Decisions & Agreements

Uploaded accreditation identity documents (photo or PDF) will be processed via OCR to auto-populate form fields, with extracted data stored as structured fields (not just the image) to support expiry tracking and renewal prompts.

- The system must validate uniqueness of key identifiers (e.g., passport number, Emirates ID) and block duplicate accreditation submissions.

Accreditation will be primarily managed via the web portal, with equivalent submission functionality also available on the mobile app as a secondary option for individual applicants.

Wherever practical, related information should be consolidated into fewer end-user-facing screens rather than mirrored across many separate boards — including accreditation-holder monitoring being treated as a filtered view within the general entitlement monitoring platform rather than a fully separate system.

Virtual queue guests must be operationally kept distinct from VIP fast-lane guests at the ride itself, to preserve the VIP guest's paid value; a dedicated handling approach (e.g., separate line or scan window) is needed for virtual-queue arrivals.

Virtual queue return-time estimates must be dynamically recalculated based on real-time conditions across all three guest tiers (walk-in, virtual queue, VIP), not fixed at time of booking.

- Virtual queue must support both a smartphone app-based flow (theme parks) and a kiosk/wristband-scan-based flow (water parks, where guests typically don't carry phones).

- The system should proactively upsell express/fast-lane tickets to guests facing long waits, balancing guest experience with venue revenue.
